name: Grimand Elmore
summary: In Stormwind City, Grimand Elmore receives Furen Longbeard's technical notes. Their brief exchange carries intricate findings between two headstrong weaponsmiths who share the city.

sections.title: A Message Across the District
sections.body: Furen Longbeard forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail and uncovered intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles. He records his findings on parchment, then asks you to deliver them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter at a nearby weapon shop.

sections.title: Professional Pride and Curiosity
sections.body: Grimand Elmore bristles at the manuscript. He insists he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows, and the thought that his former pupil could teach him wounds his pride. Yet Grimand cannot resist reading the notes. Soon he finds an intriguing idea and is eager to test it himself.

faq.answer: Grimand Elmore is a respected weaponsmith with a shop in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. He has taught craft skills to local smiths, including Furen Longbeard, and takes great pride in his work.

faq.q: Why does Furen send notes to Grimand?
faq.answer: Furen discovered new techniques while crafting the Fire Hardened Mail and recorded his methods in technical notes. He shares his findings with Grimand, though the older dwarf's fiery temper and stubborn pride may make him bristle at being taught something new.

faq.q: Where can Grimand Elmore be found?
faq.answer: Grimand Elmore works in a weapon shop in Stormwind City's Dwarven District, a short walk from Furen Longbeard's forge.

faq.q: How does Grimand react to the notes?
faq.answer: Grimand first bristles, insisting he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows. Then the master smith's curiosity takes hold when he finds an intriguing technique he wants to test.

faq.q: What happens after Grimand reads the notes?
faq.answer: Intrigued by Furen's work on fire-tempering metal, Grimand sets out on an ambitious craft project. Further tasks call for rare components with elemental heat.

faq.q: Why does Furen warn to duck when handing over the notes?
faq.answer: Furen knows Grimand's fiery temper and pride firsthand. He expects Grimand may throw a tantrum or an object at the thought that an apprentice could teach the master a new technique.

angles.text: As a warrior, you move from armoring yourself toward martial weapons forged through the same elemental experiments.
As a blacksmith, you can see in Furen and Grimand's exchange the fierce rivalry and sharing of trade secrets common among master metalworkers.
As a dwarf, you can hear in Grimand and Furen's prideful banter the competitive yet cooperative traditions of Khaz Modan's smithing culture.
